newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians arrest suspected Russian mobsters.
newsitem.headline: Italians arrest suspected Russian mobsters.

text.p: Police in Italy on Monday said they had arrested several suspected members of a Russian Mafia clan when they burst in on a "crime summit" at a swish Dolomite ski resort.
Police said the operation, led by officers of a Rome-based anti-organised crime unit, had resulted in about 15 arrests.

The suspects, most of them Russian, were arrested at a hotel in the northern winter holiday resort of Madonna di Campiglio and in raids in other parts of Italy. All faced charges of membership of a Mafia-style organisation.

Crime groups from Russia and other former Soviet republics have spread their tentacles into the West since the collapse of communism and have built operational links with organised crime in Italy and elsewhere.
Police and other experts say Italy has become a favoured location for Russian Mafias to launder the profits of drugs and arms trafficking and other operations.

Confercommercio, an Italian trade association with a good record of tracking the routes organised crime takes to recycle "dirty money", said in a recent report that Russian groups had invested huge sums in manufacturing, tourism and property.
It estimated the amount of money involved between 1993 and 1995 at around seven trillion to 10 trillion lire ($4 billion to $6 billion).
